items.prompt: White plans d4-d5. After the push, can Black win the pawn on d5?

claims.statement: After the push one black piece, the knight, attacks d5.
After the push one white piece, the rook, defends d5.
Black can bring the rook to d8: two attackers.
White can answer with Nc3: two defenders.
Along the engine line White does not lose the pawn.

hints: How many Black pieces attack d5 after the push, and how many White pieces defend it?
Which Black piece can move to a square from which it attacks d5? Which White piece can move to a square from which it defends d5?
Black can play Rd8 and White can answer Nc3: two attackers against two defenders.
items.explain: After d5, the knight on f6 attacks the pawn and the rook on d1 defends it. Black can bring the rook from f8 to d8 and White can bring the knight from b1 to c3, so it is two against two. The engine finds no way for Black to win the pawn.
